description:
South Korea’s economy is becoming dangerously tied to the global AI boom. Its biggest chipmakers now sit at the center of a financial chain connecting Seoul, Silicon Valley, Wall Street, and hundreds of billions of dollars in speculative investment.

This video explores why South Korea’s stock market has become a warning system for the entire AI industry. Samsung and SK Hynix supply the memory and semiconductor hardware powering America’s biggest tech companies, while fears over Chinese competition, falling margins, and massive AI spending are making both markets increasingly vulnerable to the same shock.
We also examine the billions being burned by companies like Alphabet, the circular investments propping up parts of the AI ecosystem, and why hundreds of thousands of leveraged Korean investors were caught in sudden market liquidations. Meanwhile, China’s push to develop its own chipmaking technology could threaten one of South Korea’s most valuable industries.
